purpose: Thirty horror, necromantic, demonic, mythical, and eldritch monsters with distinct readable mechanics, including a five-stage cannibal Gravefeeding ecology.

entities.name: Carrion Seed

identity.fantasy: A fist-sized grave organism that survives by eating dead tissue—including its own wounded broodmates—to grow replacement limbs within seconds.
identity.silhouette: Hairless quadruped no larger than a dog, with translucent abdomen, lamprey mouth, and six folding bone-spines.
identity.lore_hook: The first stage of the Gravefeeding Cycle is less a corpse-eater than a biological decision to never waste meat.

signature: Feast Instinct causes injured Seeds to drag down a critically wounded broodmate and consume it, healing the survivors while reducing total pack size.
counterplay: Burst-kill multiple Seeds before they can begin a feast; fire or area denial can interrupt the feeding channel.
evolution: Survivors that consume enough biomass during authored events can be replaced by MON-044 Broodmaws.

vfx: Consumed flesh becomes visible dark mass moving through translucent abdomens.
animation: Feeding uses frantic multi-body latch animations rather than generic melee swipes.
audio: Creature-specific positional tells for aggro, signature windup, impact, stagger, and retreat behavior.

method: Tier-I Gravefeeding outbreaks and low-level carrion nests.

entities.name: Broodmaw

identity.fantasy: A human-sized Gravefeeding predator grown from fused Carrion Seeds; it carries vestigial mouths across its torso that bite its own flesh to trigger combat mutations.
identity.silhouette: Six-limbed hyena-like body with ribcage mouths, backward antlers, and mismatched limbs grown from consumed brood.
identity.lore_hook: A Broodmaw remembers every sibling it ate as another mouth arguing inside its chest.

signature: Rib Feast bites one of its own vestigial mouths shut, sacrificing health to gain a short mutation such as armor plates or leap speed.
Biomass Claim executes a feeding leap toward fallen lesser Gravefeeding creatures to restore the sacrificed health.
counterplay: Punish self-damage during Rib Feast; deny corpse access to prevent full recovery.
evolution: A Broodmaw that wins repeated cannibal contests can become MON-045 Maw-Court Butcher.

entities.name: Maw-Court Butcher

identity.fantasy: A towering Gravefeeding butcher that breeds strength through ritualized pack cannibalism, selecting one lesser creature at a time to consume for specialized organs.
identity.silhouette: Twelve-foot upright brute with butcher-hook forearms, an exposed second spine, and a crown made from fused jawbones.
identity.lore_hook: The Maw-Court discovered hierarchy when the strongest creature realized it could choose who was eaten next.

signature: Meat Decree marks one nearby lesser Gravefeeding unit as the next sacrifice.
Organ Claim consumes the marked unit after a windup and gains one visible organ-power based on that unit's archetype.
Butcher's Law orders surviving lesser creatures to protect the newly grown organ until it is destroyed.
counterplay: Kill or separate the marked sacrifice before the consume completes; newly grown organs become visible weak points.

identity.silhouette: Cloud-long dragon with missing scales exposing miniature storms—blizzard, lightning, ash, rain, and clear vacuum patches.

entities.name: The Child Behind Thunder

identity.fantasy: An Absolute-class entity that appears as a small distant silhouette only when lightning flashes, while its real body is the entire authored storm system attacking the region.
identity.silhouette: A childlike figure far beyond the arena, visible for fractions of a second inside every lightning strike; no persistent local body.
identity.lore_hook: No one agrees whether the storm follows the Child or whether the Child is how the storm imagines itself.

signature: Seen Once makes the apparition visible in one of several distant anchors during lightning, revealing the next attack family.
Thunder Memory repeats earlier safe/unsafe patterns in altered order, rewarding observation.
Do Not Approach punishes attempts to chase the distant silhouette by redirecting players toward actual local storm objectives.
Name the Storm requires activating a sequence of grounded lightning rods matching apparition positions.
Quiet Child ends the storm-body phase and manifests a short-lived vulnerable local core only after the sequence is solved.
counterplay: Watch apparition positions, solve rod sequences, and treat the silhouette as information rather than a chase target.

vfx: Lightning briefly reveals the distant figure at impossible scale depth.
Storm clouds form subtle facial negative space only during Thunder Memory.
Rod activations draw white lines toward the sky.
Quiet Child drains all color from the clouds before the local core appears.
The vulnerable core resembles a small black thunderhead containing a single white eye.
animation: The apparition has almost no motion—only tiny posture changes between flashes.
Local objectives animate the storm rather than a body skeleton.
Quiet Child condenses cloud layers inward over several seconds.
Core defeat releases the storm upward instead of playing a conventional death fall.
